ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the attached figure shows a transmission line equivalent circuit from left to right, labeled in sequence as P1, P2, P3, P4. Between P1 and P2 is a series reactance j0.1 pu; between P2 and P3 is a series capacitor, labeled as -j0.1 pu; between P3 and P4 is again a series reactance j0.1 pu. Near the receiving end on the right end, current I = 1 pu and pf = 1 are marked, and the receiving-end voltage Vr is marked; on the left side, source voltage Vs = 1 pu∠0° is marked. Then reason: taking the load-end current I as the real-axis reference, since pf = 1, the receiving-end voltage is in phase with the current. From P4 going left through the right-side series reactance j0.1 pu to P3, it is necessary to add the inductive voltage drop j0.1I, so the P3 voltage has an added quadrature component compared with the adjacent receiving-end point, and the voltage magnitude rises. Continuing left through the midpoint series capacitor -j0.1 pu to P2, this capacitor produces an opposite voltage drop, equivalently subtracting j0.1I, causing the voltage magnitude to fall back again. The left-side reactance only connects P2 with the source side. Therefore, among these marked positions, the maximum voltage appears at P3 on the right side of the capacitor.

raw_record.question_text: In the transmission-line model shown, with a series capacitor at its mid-point, at which labeled location is the maximum voltage on the line?

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the line has P1--j0.1--P2--(-j0.1 capacitor)--P3--j0.1--P4, with I = 1 pu at unity power factor at the receiving end. Take the load-end current as the real-axis reference. Starting from P4 and moving left, add the right-line inductive drop j0.1I to get the voltage at P3, which increases the voltage magnitude above the uncompensated adjacent point. Moving further left across the series capacitor subtracts j0.1I, so the voltage at P2 drops back down. The left inductor then only relates P2 to the ideal source side. Therefore, among the line locations affected by the mid-point series capacitor, the maximum voltage occurs at P3.
method.CoT_raw: 先描述图像：附图显示一条从左到右的传输线等值电路，依次标有 P1、P2、P3、P4。P1 到 P2 之间是串联电抗 j0.1 pu，P2 到 P3 之间是串联电容，标注为 -j0.1 pu，P3 到 P4 之间又是串联电抗 j0.1 pu。右端接收端附近标有电流 I = 1 pu，pf = 1，并标出接收端电压 Vr；左侧标有源电压 Vs = 1 pu∠0°。再推理：以负载端电流 I 作为实轴参考，由于 pf = 1，接收端电压与电流同相。从 P4 向左经过右侧串联电抗 j0.1 pu 到 P3，需要加上感性压降 j0.1I，因此 P3 电压比相邻接收端点增加了正交分量，电压幅值上升。继续向左经过中点串联电容 -j0.1 pu 到 P2 时，该电容产生相反的压降，等效减去 j0.1I，使电压幅值又降回去。左侧电抗只是把 P2 与源侧相连。因而在这些标注位置中，最大电压出现在电容右侧的 P3。
method.answer_match_reason: The predicted answer is exactly the same labeled location as the standard answer.

answer_match_part_results.reason: Both identify P3 as the location of maximum voltage.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct phasor-voltage-drop route: it uses the labeled impedances and current/power-factor data to compare bus voltage magnitudes at P1–P4, rather than relying only on a qualitative statement that a series capacitor raises voltage.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the diagram as a single radial transmission path from P1 to P4 with labeled points P1, P2, P3, P4. Note the sequence of series elements: j0.1 pu between P1 and P2, a series capacitor -j0.1 pu between P2 and P3, and j0.1 pu between P3 and P4. Also read the receiving-end current annotation I = 1 pu, pf = 1, and the source/receiving voltage arrows.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text to know that the requested item is the labeled location of maximum line voltage and that the relevant special component is the series capacitor at the midpoint.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the AC phasor series-drop relation V_left - V_right = ZI. With unity power factor, take current as the real reference, so each inductive j0.1 element contributes a +j0.1 phasor rise when moving from load toward source, while the capacitor contributes the opposite sign. Compare the resulting phasor magnitudes at the labeled points; the node immediately on the receiving-side of the capacitor, P3, is where the compensating capacitor produces the local voltage peak on the line.
